chunks: Al-Husayn b. Sayf said: My brother 'Ali b. Sayf narrated to me from his father Sayf b. 'Umayra from al-Hasan b. al-Sabbah. He said: Anas b. Malik narrated to me from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family). He said:
Every obstinate tyrant is one who refuses to say "there is no god but Allah" (la ilaha illallah).

key_terms.أبى: To refuse or reject, implying willful and arrogant rejection rather than mere ignorance
key_terms.جبار عنيد: An obstinate tyrant, a Quranic term (14:15, 11:59) describing those who arrogantly reject divine guidance
key_terms.لا إله إلا الله: The declaration of divine unity (tahlil/shahada), the most fundamental statement in Islam

ai.seo_question: Who is the obstinate tyrant (jabbar anid) according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This Prophetic tradition, transmitted through a chain of narrators ending with the companion Anas b. Malik, defines the Quranic term 'jabbar anid' (obstinate tyrant) as one who refuses to declare the unity of God. The hadith connects the Quranic description of arrogant disbelievers with the specific act of rejecting the shahada, the most fundamental expression of monotheism.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Sayf said: My brother `Ali b. Sayf narrated to me from his father Sayf b. `Umayra from al-Hasan b. Al-Sabah. He said: Anas b. Malik narrated to me from the Prophet (s). He said:
Every obstinate tyrant is one who refuses to say: “there is no god but Allah” (la ilaha illallah).
